# Spec 001 -- unified web interface: demo evidence (screenshots)

Captured 2026-09-20 (local evening; timestamps inside the pages are UTC
2026-09-21T03:5x) on the Linux node, from the `civsim_web` app installed at
`.venv/bin/civsim-web`, working tree at commit `c96bb1b` plus uncommitted
changes that do not touch `src/civsim_web/`.

**Read this first: what data is on these pages.**

- Every run, turn, step, event, yield and configuration shown here is
  **synthetic fixture data**, generated by `tests/web_support/fixtures.py`
  (`make_store()`, `make_catalog_store()`, `make_event()`). Nothing on these
  pages came from a real Civilization VI game. The run ids (`run-live`,
  `run-live-2`, `run-01`..`run-05`), the yields (straight lines), the timestamps
  (`2026-09-20T12:0x:00Z`) and the reasoning text are all fixture values.
- The **screen captures are real**: the fixtures' capture blobs are an 8-byte
  PNG signature (which renders as a broken image), so every capture with
  `screening_status == "screened_clean"` had its blob replaced in-process with
  `specs/002-civ-playing-harness/spikes/demo-evidence-linux/keyframe_1_t054s.png`,
  a genuine 720x450 window-scoped frame the 002 harness took of the Civ VI main
  menu. So the picture in each capture slot is a real harness frame, but it is
  the *same* frame everywhere and it does not correspond to the fixture turn it
  sits under.
- The one real `MatchStore` on this box (`civsim-match-store.db` at the repo
  root) was **not** used. It was in use by a live harness run while these shots
  were taken, and per that session it currently holds a single paused run from
  tonight's live demo -- a one-run, few-turns store that would not exercise the
  catalog, comparison, replay-attempt or gap pages at all. Wiring the real store
  in later is a `--store module:attr` change, nothing in the UI.

## How it was produced

Launcher (kept in the session scratchpad, not the repo; reproduced here in
full so it can be re-run): `demo_launcher.py` builds one in-process
`FakeMatchStore` (`src/civsim_web/store_client/fake.py`) that merges:

| Part | Built by | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| `run-live` | `make_store(run_id="run-live", turns=12, step_count=3, replayed_turns=[7], gap_turns=[9], withheld_capture_turns=[5], events=[9 events])` | lifecycle `playing`; turn 7 has attempt 0 (abandoned) and attempt 1 (authoritative); turn 9 has no record at all (a gap); turn 5's captures are withheld |
| `run-live-2` | `make_store(run_id="run-live-2", turns=4)` | a second `playing` run so `/` renders a list instead of 307-redirecting to the single live run |
| `run-01`..`run-05` | `make_catalog_store(completeness={"run-03": "has_gaps"}, turn_gaps={"run-03": [4]})` | five `finished` runs x 8 turns; run-03 quarantined |

then serves it with `uvicorn.run(create_app(store=store, bind_addresses=["127.0.0.1"], panels_dir=REPO/panels), host="127.0.0.1", port=8420)`.

```sh
cd /home/matt/CivSolver
PYTHONPATH=/home/matt/CivSolver .venv/bin/python <scratch>/demo_launcher.py &
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8420/healthz   # 200
```

The equivalent using only the shipped CLI (no real images, no merged catalog):

```sh
PYTHONPATH=/home/matt/CivSolver .venv/bin/civsim-web \
  --store tests.web_support.fixtures:make_store --bind 127.0.0.1 serve
```

Browser: **Chromium 153.0.8010.36** (`/usr/bin/chromium`), headless:

```sh
chromium --headless=new --disable-gpu --no-sandbox --hide-scrollbars \
  --window-size=1440,1000 --virtual-time-budget=4000 --screenshot=<out.png> <url>
```

Screenshots are viewport crops (1440x1000, or 1440x2600 for the `*-tall`
variants, 420x900 for the `*-mobile-420` variants), not full-page captures.
Pages longer than the viewport are cut off at the bottom; that is the
screenshot, not the page.

Nothing was installed. No source file was modified. The Civ VI client, the
tuner port and `civsim-match-store.db` were not touched.

## Honest visual notes

Screenshots I looked at pixel-by-pixel: 01, 02, 04 (three separate captures),
04b, 05b, 06, 06b, 07, 09, 10, 11, 12, 13, 13b, 15, 16, 17, 18. Files 03, 05,
08, 12b and 14 were verified only by HTTP status, content type and non-trivial
file size; I did not open them.

### Things that are wrong or misleading

1. **"connection lost -- this view may be stale" is always shown on the live
   view, even when the connection is fine.** This is a CSS bug, not a capture
   artefact. `src/civsim_web/templates/live/run_detail.html:56` renders the
   marker with the `hidden` attribute, and `static/poll.js:46-52,158-168` only
   un-hides it after two consecutive failed polls -- I verified with
   `chromium --dump-dom` after JS ran that the root has `data-stale="false"`
   and the span still has `hidden=""`. But `src/civsim_web/static/style.css:92`
   is `.stale-marker { display: block; ... }`, and an author `display` rule
   overrides the user-agent `[hidden] { display: none }`. Net effect: the
   warning text is visible on every load of `/runs/<id>` (04, 04b, 17), while
   the orange glance border that `[data-stale="true"]` would add is correctly
   absent. Reproduced identically with and without `--virtual-time-budget`,
   and with the page held open for real polls (server log shows the poll
   returning 200). One-line fix: add `.stale-marker[hidden] { display: none; }`
   (or `[hidden] { display: none !important; }`).
2. **The live-view glance card overflows at phone width** (17). `style.css:65`
   gives `.glance` fixed minimum columns (`minmax(16rem,1fr) auto
   minmax(20rem,2fr) auto`, i.e. at least ~36rem = 576px) and there is no
   `@media` rule anywhere in `style.css`, so at 420px the LAST DECISION and
   LAST CONFIRMED columns are clipped off the right edge ("LAS", "Fo", "Sci Ca
   to" are visible fragments). Everything below the card stacks fine.
3. **Duplicate "1" in the turn Jump list** (05, 05b, 06, 06b: "Jump: 1 1 2 4 5
   6 7 8"). `templates/history/turn_replay.html:74` emits an unconditional link
   to turn 1, then the loop on line 75 (`range(max(turn-5,1), turn+6)`) emits
   turn 1 again whenever the current turn is <= 6. Cosmetic; both links work.
4. **Placeholder rows on populated pages.** The generic view-model renderer
   prints `Empty state --`, `Listing limitation --`, `Active filters --`,
   `Requested but unrecorded --`, `Divergence points --`, `Unavailable
   fields --` as literal rows even when there is nothing to say (01, 02, 04,
   11, 12, 13). This is the UP-005 "absent is shown as absent" rule applied
   literally; it reads as noise on a page that has data. On the 404 page the
   first row is `Error: error` because the error view model literally carries
   `"error": "error"` (see `turn-9-gap-404.json`); the informative field is
   `"kind": "turn_gap"`, which the HTML page does not show as a row.
5. **Same real frame everywhere.** Every capture slot shows the identical Civ VI
   main-menu frame (see the data note at the top). That is a limitation of
   this evidence set, not of the UI -- the UI serves whatever bytes the store
   returns.

### Things that look right

- Real PNG bytes served through `/captures/{id}/image` render as a proper
  image in the live view, the replay, the step page and the panel route; the
  8-byte fixture blobs would have shown a broken image.
- The gap turn is refused with a 404 that explains itself (10), the metric
  charts break their line at the gap and mark it with a dashed red rule
  (05, 12b), the catalog and comparison quarantine the gapped runs with a
  stated reason (02, 13), and the superseded attempt stays reachable with a
  banner pointing at the authoritative one (07 vs 08). Principle III/IV
  reasoning is spelled out in prose on every page that applies it.
- Every route also answers as JSON with the same field names the HTML shows
  (`run-live.json`, `healthz.json`, `turn-9-gap-404.json`), and the 404 is a
  structured JSON error, not an HTML-only page.
- No external requests: Chromium made requests only to 127.0.0.1:8420
  (page, `/static/style.css`, `/static/poll.js`, capture images, and a
  `/favicon.ico` that 404s harmlessly). No webfonts, no CDN.
- The dark theme, monospace values and left colour bars are consistent across
  all pages; nothing rendered with missing styles.

### Not exercised here

`/runs/{id}/turns/{n}/steps/{i}/panels/{panel_id}`, `?page=` on the catalog,
`?series=` on metrics, `&metrics=` on compare, the withheld-capture rendering
(turn 5 exists in the fixture but no screenshot of it was taken), the
`published_port_only` store shape, and a store that is unreachable (503 path).
